correctness.rationale: Under probability-normalized area, integrals of the exponential and first coordinate moments are j0 and i j1 u; the degree-1 projection coefficient is 3i j1 u. j0 and j1 cannot vanish together. Dividing by nonzero j0 identifies complex projective lines exactly with the real vector Y=(1/z-cot z)u. h′=csc²(z)−1/z²>0 on each non-pole band and has the stated endpoint limits, giving the sharp closed-ball threshold κR<π, higher-band paired solutions, special j1=0 spheres, and unoriented directions on j0=0 shells. The sine-product expansion for z<π gives h(z)/z≥1/3 and h′(z)≥1/3. The symmetric radial Jacobian of Y is ≥κ/3, and integration over the convex ball proves |x−x′|≤3|Y(x)−Y(x′)|/κ; h(z)~z/3 proves sharpness. Scaling columns of (1,3iY) verifies rank 1+affine dimension, and the cross-product identity verifies the exact two-column Gram determinant. Examined the packaged quadrature/finite-alias checker and separately checked formula and boundary logic; sampled tests cannot prove continuum claims.
